identification: Telegram remote-control daemon for Claude Code CLI sessions in dtach
marker_line: aipager 1.3.7: translation key misread as cleanup; benign file sends

comparison.baseline_reproduction: The same suspicious translation-key detection also fires on 1.3.6 with the initial current rules.

decisive_evidence: update_flow.py:387 passes upd.marker.done as the key to Plural, not as a filesystem path. deliver_update_marker uses it to render the update-complete notification for the requesting chat.
self_update.py writes a private JSON restart handoff marker, then reads and clears it to avoid duplicate update-complete messages. These implementations are unchanged from 1.3.6.

1.3.7 adds claude_launch.py, send_check.py, media_kind.py, bot/outbox.py and bot/claude_bidi.py. These enable SendUserFile and improve file delivery, session state and text display; existing dependencies and update machinery are unchanged.

SendUserFile requests pass PreToolUse checks, secret-name and credential-directory blocks, member-root restrictions, opened-file identity checks and transcript verification. notify._verified_batches sends only verified batches to the session chat, never an embedded recipient.
The large static/_app.py string is readable JavaScript served as the Mini App UI. It is byte-identical to the prior release, not an encoded executable.

peer_auth._environ_has reads a candidate ancestor environment to verify CLAUDE_DTACH_SESSION, not to harvest credentials. tunnel.detect_public_url looks up tailscale and queries status, not debug prefs.
set_target calls select session targets; cancel_scheduled_restart cancels an update restart. Neither establishes DoS or persistence.
bot/outbox._opened_path uses /proc/self/fd and readlink to verify the source file location before copying. There is no memfd activation on this path.
